strategies.rationale: The broadest route. Expected to be high volume and low yield; it exists as the baseline the narrower routes have to beat.
Aims straight at the JA half of the pair the checker needs, at the cost of catching translation projects that ship no product.
Engine-scoped. Unity projects usually keep locale data as JSON or CSV in-repo, which is what the inventory can see.
Engine-scoped. Godot's own tooling prefers CSV, so this route is expected to produce DETECTED_BUT_UNSUPPORTED more often than scannable pairs - which is itself worth measuring.
Visual novels are localization-heavy by construction and frequently ship Japanese.
RPG Maker projects often carry JSON locale data and a Japanese original.
Topic-scoped rather than text-scoped: narrower, and the repositories that self-label are more likely to own their localization.
Looks for parties who already treat locale defects as a mechanical problem - the workflow axis rather than the problem axis.
